name: RealsleyHook
description: A pool for checked accounts only. Only an account that holds this hook's credential in the registry named at deployment may swap on the pool or add liquidity to it; removing liquidity is never gated, so an account whose credential is withdrawn can always take its funds out. Meant for an asset only people who have passed a check may hold. It gates this pool, not the asset. It moves no funds and has no owner.

reasons: No dynamic fee and no returns-delta flag, so a general router finds the pool.
But a swap is refused unless it comes through the router named at deployment from a credential holder, so a general router cannot trade on it.
The 0x91 address-prefix rule applies to a deployed address. This hook is not deployed.

pool.binding: None. Any pool may name this hook.
pool.fee: Any. The hook does not read or set the fee.

deltas.returns: BeforeSwapDelta 0, fee override 0, or a revert

externalCalls.target: the one router named at deployment
externalCalls.why: Only this address is asked who the swapper is. In try/catch: a router that reverts means nobody is recognised.
Names the holder of the position liquidity is added to. Not wrapped: if it reverts, the deposit reverts.
Asks whether the account has passed the check. Not wrapped: for a gate, a check that cannot be made is a refusal.

securityAssumptions: Assumes the v4 `PoolManager` is the only caller of the callbacks (enforced by the `onlyPoolManager` modifier inherited from `BaseHook`).
Assumes the router named at deployment answers `msgSender()` with the account that called it. A router that lies makes every statement here about 'the swapper' false.
Assumes the PositionManager named at deployment is the official one: it sets a position's salt to its token id and its `ownerOf` names the holder.
Assumes the registry named at deployment tells the truth and stays available. Whoever controls it controls what this hook decides.
doesNotGuarantee: Does not gate removing liquidity or donating: funds can always be taken out.
Does not know whose money a swap spends: it knows who called the router named at deployment and who holds a position.
Does not let anyone swap through any other router: such a swapper cannot be established and is refused.
Does not stop a position's NFT being transferred to someone not allowed, who then holds it and earns its fees but cannot add to it.
Does not gate the asset itself: the token can still be transferred or traded anywhere else.
Does not let anyone swap while the registry is unavailable.

invariants.statement: The hook's address carries exactly the permissions it declares: beforeAddLiquidity and beforeSwap, mask 0x880.
The constructor rejects an address with one bit different.
A checked account swaps and anyone else is refused.
A credential withdrawn stops the next swap and deposit, but never the way out.
A registry that reverts refuses every swap.
Nobody can open a position for an unchecked account.
